title: Generic helpers
description:
Write generic functions and a generic class:

```typescript
function uniqueBy<T, K>(items: readonly T[], key: (item: T) => K): T[]
function pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(items: readonly T[], key: K): T[K][]
function indexBy<T, K extends keyof T>(items: readonly T[], key: K): Map<T[K], T>

class Cache<K, V> {
  constructor(capacity: number)
  get(key: K): V | undefined
  set(key: K, value: V): void
  get size(): number
}
```

- `uniqueBy` keeps the **first** item for each key, in order.
- `indexBy` maps each item's `key` value to the item; later items replace earlier ones with the same value.
- `Cache` holds at most `capacity` entries. When a new key is set while it is full, the **least recently used** entry is dropped. Both `get` (of a key that is there) and `set` count as using a key.
hints: A `Map` remembers insertion order. Deleting and setting a key again moves it to the end, so the first key is always the least recently used.
`this.#entries.keys().next().value` is the first key in the Map.
rules: Give uniqueBy the type parameters <T, K>.
Constrain pluck's key with K extends keyof T.
Give pluck the return type T[K][].
Make Cache generic: class Cache<K, V>.
